title: Vacuum Runtime Log Failure Rate
dataSources: Roborock sessions (`roborock:session`), Tidy schedules (`tidy:schedule`), cleaning checklists (`cleaning:checklist`), and vacuum runtime logs (`vacuum:runtime`).
app: Roborock vacuum session exports, Tidy scheduling logs, cleaning checklists, and runtime telemetry from robot vacuums ingested into Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=vacuum:runtime
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(runtime_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by device_name
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often vacuum runtime log records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each device.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize runtime_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per device.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It turns which parts of your vacuum runtime log data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
